meta.name: Soft Editorial Collage Design System
meta.intent: High-level design direction for reproducing the attached reference aesthetic across the app.
meta.productContext: A personal wealth and investing app that should feel warm, editorial, playful, premium, and approachable instead of cold fintech.

brandEssence.feeling: The UI should feel like a carefully art-directed lifestyle product, not a utilitarian finance dashboard. It should suggest clarity, warmth, and delight through soft color fields, large rounded cards, generous negative space, and layered compositions.
brandEssence.designPrinciple: Use bright pastel surfaces and editorial composition to make finance feel emotionally safe and visually memorable.

creativeDirection.overallLook: Large soft cards float on a warm off-white canvas. Layouts feel editorial and asymmetrical but still balanced. Surfaces use broad pastel gradients or single-tone pastel fills. Components often feel like printed cards or objects placed on a tabletop.
creativeDirection.visualMetaphor: Think modern greeting-card app, magazine layout, and lifestyle brand art direction translated into a finance product.
personalityRules: Prefer one strong focal area per screen.
Prefer clear hierarchy over showing everything at once.
Prefer soft delight over hard enterprise sharpness.
Make data feel friendly without reducing trust.

screenComposition.background: Use a warm neutral page background rather than pure white. Default should feel creamy, airy, and quiet.
screenComposition.sections: Break screens into large rounded modules. Each module should read as a self-contained story block.
screenComposition.layoutStyle: Favor a magazine-like grid: one dominant card plus supporting cards. Allow intentional asymmetry, but maintain visual equilibrium.
screenComposition.density: Low to medium density. Do not cram multiple explanations, labels, and controls into the same visible region.

spacing.philosophy: Spacing should feel generous and breathable. The app should never feel crowded.
spacing.cardPadding: 16-24px inside cards depending on content depth.
spacing.microSpacing: 6-12px between related text lines, chips, or compact controls.

shapeLanguage.secondaryRadius: 16-22px for inner trays, pills, sheets, and compact surfaces.
shapeLanguage.pillStyle: Rounded, friendly, thick enough to feel tactile.

colorSystem.strategy: Use a quiet neutral canvas plus cheerful pastel statement colors. Each large block may own a color mood.

pageBackground.description: Warm off-white / cream, slightly tinted rather than stark white.

usageRules: Do not use too many saturated colors in the same module.
Let color blocks do the emotional work; keep chrome minimal.
Finance-specific status colors should still exist, but soften them slightly to fit the world.

typography.direction: Pair an editorial serif-like display style for major headings with a clean, rounded, modern sans-serif for body, controls, metrics, and utility text.

headlineStyle.tone: Confident, elegant, slightly nostalgic editorial headlines.
headlineStyle.usage: Hero titles, section titles, major card headings.

bodyStyle.usage: Descriptions, supporting text, labels, helper content.

rules: Use few font sizes, but with strong hierarchy.
Headlines should feel oversized and intentional.
Descriptions should remain concise and not form large gray paragraphs.
Numbers should be crisp, prominent, and easy to compare.

cardStyle.look: Chunky rounded rectangles with soft fill, subtle shadow, and a sense of physical presence.
cardStyle.shadow: Soft, low-contrast, diffused shadow; never harsh or heavy.
cardStyle.border: Usually no visible border, or an extremely soft hairline if needed.
cardStyle.layering: Allow object overlap, like a white tray or floating panel sitting on top of a colored card.

innerPanels.look: White trays, mini sheets, or inset modules used inside colorful cards.
innerPanels.shadow: Small but noticeable lift to imply physical stacking.

imageryAndIllustration.style: Collage, mockup-like product imagery, tilted cards, layered screenshots, small floating objects, and tactile visual inserts.
imageryAndIllustration.guideline: If using artwork or screenshots, present them as composition elements, not full-bleed content blocks.
imageryAndIllustration.forThisApp: Charts, account cards, summaries, and goal cards can be treated like art-directed objects placed onto a pastel board.

appShell.topBar: Minimal chrome. Use lots of breathing room. Icons may sit in soft circular or rounded containers.
appShell.bottomNavigation: Use a rounded floating tray rather than a hard edge tab bar when possible. Background should feel elevated and friendly.

heroCards.purpose: Introduce the most important message or metric on a screen.
heroCards.design: Large pastel card with strong title, short supporting copy, and possibly a layered object or inset tray.
heroCards.contentRule: One hero metric or one key story only.

summaryMetricCards.look: Compact inner white trays or mini pastel blocks with strong numeric emphasis.

sectionCards.look: Rounded modules with clear top-left title and lightweight body structure.
sectionCards.rule: Avoid heavy visual dividers. Use spacing, tint, and alignment instead.

buttons.primary: Rounded, bold, high contrast, simple text, feels touchable and slightly chunky.
buttons.secondary: Pill or soft-outline button with tinted fill.
buttons.ghost: Text or icon button with minimal chrome.

chipsAndFilters.look: Rounded capsules with clear selected and unselected states.
chipsAndFilters.selectedState: Use full category color or a stronger tint.
chipsAndFilters.unselectedState: Use soft tinted fills rather than gray pills.
chipsAndFilters.layout: Center align chip groups where possible. They should feel balanced, not left-heavy.

cardsForCharts.look: Charts should sit inside calm, refined cards. Supporting controls should be lightweight.
cardsForCharts.axes: Axes should be subtle and not dominate the module.
cardsForCharts.labels: Short, sparse, readable at a glance.
cardsForCharts.annotations: Prefer a few well-placed highlights over many legends and long explanations.

dataTablesAndLists.approach: Convert dense data into soft panels. Use scrollable trays with fixed headers if needed.
dataTablesAndLists.density: Keep rows readable; do not make the table feel spreadsheet-like.

forms.inputShape: Rounded inputs with soft fill or light outline.
forms.fieldLayout: Show only essential helper text. Prefer progressive disclosure over many visible explanations.
forms.selectionControls: Use chips, dropdown sheets, or rounded segmented controls.

modalsAndSheets.look: Rounded sheet surfaces with generous top padding and minimal decoration.
modalsAndSheets.tone: Feels like a premium card sliding over the page.

goalCards.priority: Progress visualization should be friendly, not clinical.
goalCards.style: Prefer rings, progress bars, and concise labels inside cheerful surfaces.

emptyStates.content: Short sentence only. No long instructional blocks.

trust: Data should remain legible and trustworthy even inside a playful system.
Critical financial numbers must have stronger contrast than decorative text.
Performance colors should remain intuitive: green positive, red negative, amber warning.
whatToSimplify: Reduce explanatory helper text by default.
Use grouping, chips, and modular cards to avoid overwhelming the user.
Show one primary metric per card, not a wall of metrics.
howToMakeChartsFit: Place legends into existing controls when possible instead of adding separate legend blocks.
Prefer direct labeling near meaningful lines or points.

motion.philosophy: Motion should feel soft, buoyant, and premium. No snappy enterprise motion.
rules: Use gentle fade, lift, and slide transitions.
Pressed states should slightly dim or compress.
Hover or selection should feel like a tactile state change, not a technical toggle.

do: Use large rounded cards with generous whitespace.
Let color blocks define sections and mood.
Use editorial headings and short body copy.
Create focal points through scale and spacing.
Treat UI like art direction, not only layout.
dont: Do not use cold grayscale dashboards as the dominant look.
Do not overfill screens with helper text and secondary explanation.
Do not stack too many bordered boxes inside each other.
Do not use sharp corners, harsh shadows, or ultra-dense tables.
Do not make every component visually equal.

themeTokens.tokenStrategy: These tokens are intended to map directly onto this app's current theme architecture, especially `lib/app-palette.ts`, while shifting the product closer to the editorial pastel direction.

semanticColorRoles.surfaceInset: Soft white tray inside colorful cards.
semanticColorRoles.textPrimary: Main readable copy and key metrics.
semanticColorRoles.textMuted: Quiet helper text; should be used sparingly.
semanticColorRoles.accentPrimary: Primary text/action/accent for the current palette.
semanticColorRoles.tabBarBorder: Soft border with very low contrast.

input.backgroundStrategy: Prefer white or slightly tinted fill over stark outlined controls.

chartCard.annotationStyle: direct labels near lines or points

appSpecificPaletteGuidance.recommendedBasePalette: Use the existing palette system, but bias future palettes toward warm cream backgrounds with one dominant pastel card color and one deep editorial text color.

mappingToCurrentThemeShape.pageBg: Keep soft and airy. Prefer cream or very light pastel rather than saturated full-screen backgrounds.
mappingToCurrentThemeShape.primary: Use as the main editorial text/action tone, not as the only brand color.
mappingToCurrentThemeShape.categoryAccents: Should be distinct, soft-but-clear colors suitable for chips, chart points, and category ribbons.
mappingToCurrentThemeShape.folderListBg: Treat as an inset tray tint, not a loud highlight.
mappingToCurrentThemeShape.chartLine: Should usually align with primary or a slightly brighter companion accent.
mappingToCurrentThemeShape.chartFillTop: Soft translucent wash, never heavy or muddy.
mappingToCurrentThemeShape.goalRingColors: Should feel coordinated, pastel, and collectible rather than purely functional.

paletteFormula.2: Choose one deep editorial text color.
paletteFormula.3: Choose 3-5 pastel accents with distinct roles.
paletteFormula.4: Make sure charts remain readable over decorative softness.
paletteFormula.5: Avoid using two equally dominant saturated hues on the same screen.

distribution.legendStrategy: merge legend into filters or labels when possible

returns.table: insetTray + fixed header + vertical scroll body

forms.pickerStyle: rounded sheet or rounded select row

strictRulesForAIImplementation: Do not introduce flat enterprise blue-gray styling.
Do not use small radii for major cards.
Do not overuse muted helper text.
Do not make chart legends separate if the same information can live in chips or direct labels.
Do not place dense data directly on the page background; wrap it in white or lightly tinted trays.
Always preserve strong contrast for money, return, and net worth figures.

priorityOrder: 1. Start from warm neutral background and oversized rounded cards.
2. Assign each major module a pastel mood.
3. Use strong editorial typography for headings.
4. Keep body copy short and friendly.
5. Use white inset trays for dense or interactive content.
6. Merge legends into filters, chips, or direct labels whenever possible.
whenDesigningNewScreens: First decide the hero card and its color mood.
Then place 1-3 supporting modules beneath it.
If a section feels too dense, split it into cards instead of shrinking everything.
If something is decorative and data-heavy at the same time, simplify the data layer first.
implementationNotesForAI.visualTarget: A warm editorial finance product with pastel modular cards, tactile rounded surfaces, and carefully controlled information density.
